scope: Static exact private proposal review only; no production application, test execution or runtime measurement.

engine_changed_methods._refresh: Returns first member of internal tuple; public refresh/rebuild retain GraphRefreshResult.
engine_changed_methods._refresh_locked: Return annotation and all three returns become(result,status); every original statement/guard unchanged.

risks_and_limits: Git status/source observation remains best-effort against external Git/file mutations, as before; graph lock does not make repository filesystem changes atomic.
Private _refresh_locked return signature changes; no outside src/test callsite was found.
Custom graph-engine subclasses/monkeypatches overriding only refresh do not govern inherited refresh_with_status; builder currently constructs its own engine and public Git injection is preserved.
One duplicate injected git.status is removed per context build, but latency magnitude and browser deadline cure are unmeasured.
The new method is additive; no public data model field or persistence format changes.
required_focused_validation: Cold/full-build tuple and unchanged public result serialization
Exactly one injected source-status call per context
Full dirty-path freshness including ignored/non-graph-indexed extensions and non-orqalis files
Worktree source and canonical store separation plus unrelated-repository denial
Invalid digest/data and policy errors still propagate/rebuild as before
Concurrent callers receive their own local status tuple without cross-request mixups
findings: No concrete integrity defect found within this exact proposal; meaningful focused validation and fresh source qualification are required after any application.
